Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE....

A fantastic bowling performance by Ireland and they will be the happier side at the moment. They were consistent right through the innings. The good thing they did is they held onto the chances that came their way. Right from the start they were disciplined and they got their rewards. Anything under 250 is a solid thing for Ireland and they will be confident to chase this down. Now they need a good start. If dew kicks in and the openers give them a good start, we believe Ireland can level the series. Join us back for the chase in a while.

Afghanistan have crawled their way to this total! The openers laid a solid foundation, Rahmanullah Gurbaz again looked in the mood for a big score but Afghanistan lost three wickets on a trot including of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and that forced them to go in a hush mode. Mohammad Nabi and Hashmatullah Shahidi had to go defensive for a long time. They played through the middle phase, knocked it around and almost added around 100 runs. Hashmatullah Shahidi got to his fifty but Nabi fell 2 short. However, in the last 10 overs when it was time to launch, Afghanistan lost the set batters and have ended with a moderate total here.
SIX! We have a boundary! Massive! A full toss, a bit high, around off and Naveed Zadran swings and connects it over point for a biggie. Afghanistan end with 236/9.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran to open for Afghanistan. Mark Adair to bowl first. Two slips in place. Let's go...

Hashmatullah Shahidi says they would have batted first, the wicket looks good. Adds today is an important game and they will try their best. Shares it looks like the same pitch, hopes dew helps them later on. Informs about the changes.

Paul Stirling says they'll bowl. Adds they did well in the last match but didn't bat well in few patches. Reckons the series is on the line and it is a big day for them. Informs about the team changes.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Ibrahim Zadran (C), Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi, Ikram Alikhil (WK), Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Nangeyalia Kharote, Naveed Zadran, Fazalhaq Farooqi, AM Ghazanfar.

TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and will BOWL.

It's time for the third and find ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland. Due to torrential rain, the second game was abandoned and as a result, Afghanistan led the series. Ireland have a chance though to level the series but they need a better performance than the first game. Chasing more than 300, only Harry Tector and Lorcan Tucker stood up for them. Even their bowling was under par. To salvage something from this series, Ireland have to show some fight. Can they do it though? Stay tuned for toss and other updates.
...MATCH DAY...

Amidst a flurry of cricketing battles worldwide, all eyes are now fixed on the thrilling three-match ODI series between Afghanistan and Ireland at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Afghanistan dominated the first encounter, but a washout in the second match left both teams hungry for victory in the decider. With the weather favoring clear skies, Ireland sees this as their chance to level the series and make a statement. Rahmanullah Gurbaz's explosive century in the opening game set the stage on fire, while his partner Ibrahim Zadran provided invaluable support, laying the groundwork with a formidable 150-run partnership. With skillful batters like Azmatullah Omarzai, Rahmat Shah, and Mohammad Nabi in the lineup, Afghanistan boasts a solid middle order, while skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi's blazing form adds to the firepower. Their bowling arsenal, led by the fiery Fazalhaq Farooqi, proved lethal in the previous match, and the debutant AM Ghazanfar spinner showcased his potential, leaving the Irish batters on the edge. Noor Ahmad and Nabi adds their experience to support the spin arsenal. Meanwhile, Ireland knows they need to up their game in all departments to challenge the Afghans. Their top order faltered in the chase during the first match, putting pressure on stalwarts like Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie to deliver. Harry Tector's sublime century kept their hopes alive, but they'll be looking for more contributions from Curtis Campher and George Dockrell in the lower order. Bowlers like Graham Hume and Mark Adair will be key to exploiting early opportunities with the new ball, while Craig Young and Theo van Woerkom must tighten the screws in the middle overs. With the series already slipping away, Ireland aims to salvage pride by drawing level. Despite their historical struggles against Afghanistan, they are determined to rewrite the script this time. Brace yourselves for an electrifying showdown as these two cricketing powerhouses clash once again.
